newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM to decide soon on possible fare hike.
newsitem.headline: KLM to decide soon on possible fare hike.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Wednesday it would decide shortly whether to hike tariffs to offset spiralling fuel prices.
"We are still deliberating...a definitive decision can be expected shortly," KLM spokesman Peter Wellhuner said.
Wellhuner was commenting on British Airways' decision to hike European fares by 2.5 percent on average from the middle of October. BA is also mulling increases on long-haul routes.
British Airways said on Wednesday the rise in Europe was a direct consequence of the soaring cost of jet fuel, which has risen by 30 percent since the middle of July.
Wellhuner said KLM was also smarting from the increase in fuel prices, which have jumped by some 30 percent since mid-July. "We are certainly feeling it too," he said.
Earlier this month the Dutch carrier said it was considering raising its tariffs but was reluctant to go it alone.
KLM's charter units Transavia and Martinair said on Tuesday they were introducing a fuel surcharge on winter bookings.

The surcharge, which takes effect today, applies to new bookings with departures from November 1 through March 31 next year. The size of the surcharge varies according to destination, and does not apply to intercontinental routes.
KLM owns 80 percent of Transavia and holds a 50 percent stake in Martinair. Dutch charter airline Air Holland is also to hike fares.
